Основная цель данного задания – разобрат: The main goal of this task is to understand the principles of operation of an electronic multimeter in various modes.
Оценка погрешностей в данной работе не т: Error estimation is not required in this work!
Поместите в тарелку два различных металл: Place two different metal cylinders in the dish, to which the multimeter leads are connected. The distance between the cylinders should be {#0}–{#1} cm. If the cylinder has no hook, connect it using tightly wound wire. Pour salt solution into the dish so that its level is approximately {0} – {#2} cm. For each measurement, wait until the multimeter readings approximately stabilize; this takes about {#3} min. Perform all measurements with two polarities of device connection — for this, it is enough to swap the wires connected to the multimeter sockets.
Прикрепите две одинаковые пластинки к ст: Attach two identical plates to the walls of the cup using "crocodile" clips. Pour salt solution into the cup. The solution should partially cover the plates but not touch the clips.
Электронный мультиметр – цифровой прибор: An electronic multimeter is a digital device for measuring various characteristics of electrical circuits, mainly voltage, current, and resistance. The multimeter contains rather complex electronic circuits that convert input current characteristics. You do not need to know these circuits and their principles of operation in detail. You only need to know the following:
в любом режиме работы реально проводится: in any operating mode, a voltage measurement is actually performed on some internal resistor, and the obtained voltage value is then "converted" into the required measured quantity;
в режиме измерения сопротивлений мультим: in resistance measurement mode, the multimeter has an internal voltage source;
для измерения напряжения внутренний исто: no internal source is needed for voltage measurement;
при протекании тока через растворы элект: various galvanic effects occur when current flows through electrolyte solutions.
